study_families.study_label: MoTrPAC Pre-COVID (pre-suspension) Human Blood Study — baseline acute exercise bout
study_families.design: Randomized, parallel-group, controlled acute-exercise study (3 arms: endurance exercise [EE], resistance exercise [RE], non-exercise control [CON]) nested within a larger exercise-training RCT; this report analyzes only the pre-intervention baseline acute bout. A post-training acute-bout repeat (n=44/175) was collected but excluded from analysis here.
study_families.training_load: Parent MoTrPAC protocol included 12 weeks of supervised exercise training (EE/RE) or control following the baseline acute test; only 45/176 (26%) completed the post-intervention follow-up acute test before COVID-19 suspension, and those data (44 with biospecimens) are not analyzed in this report.
study_families.cointerventions: Participants instructed to standardize COX-inhibitor, biotin, caffeine, alcohol, exercise and final-nutrition exposure before the acute test; exact protocol detailed only in a companion paper (Clinical Landscape, in submission) not retrieved for this pilot.
study_families.study_notes: Companion papers referenced throughout but not retrieved for this pilot: Clinical Landscape (in submission), Multi-Omic Landscape (in submission), Skeletal Muscle companion, Adipose Tissue companion (all REF, in submission/preparation). Same MoTrPAC pre-COVID cohort underlies all of them.

reports.inclusion_reason: Identifiable single acute exercise bout (endurance or resistance cycling/resistance circuit) in adults, pre-exercise baseline plus multiple post-exercise blood samples up to 24 h (within the 0-72h organising window), concurrent non-exercise control arm; immune-linked measurements present via a dedicated immune-cell transcriptomic enrichment/deconvolution analysis and named immune mediator proteins (p.5 Abstract: '... differences in immune cell responses ...'; p.14 Results heading 'Resistance exercise leads to greater innate immune cellular responses'; p.22 STAR Methods, Acute Exercise Intervention/Biospecimen Collection).
reports.reviewer_notes: Full-text screening disposition fields are out of scope for this charting-only pilot task (the 10-report charting pilot is separate from the 50-record screening-consistency pilot per PILOT_README §1/§5); set to NA rather than NR because no screening step was attempted here, not because a screening result is missing. Charting-purpose eligibility opinion is recorded in the top-level eligibility_opinion field.
reports.author_stated_use: mechanistic_research — authors frame the goal as describing 'large-scale plasma proteomic, metabolomic, and whole blood transcriptional profiling' to 'characterize the multi-omic responses to acute exercise in the circulation' and to 'provide a new resource for the scientific community'; no clinical, monitoring, return-to-training or infection-risk use is proposed for any specific immune marker in this report.
author_window_interpretation_locator: Full-text search of the pdftotext extraction of R19_PMC12980391.2.pdf for 'open window', 'immunosuppression', 'susceptibility' and 'redistribution' returned no matches in Abstract, Results or Discussion; authors instead frame post-exercise immune changes as cellular 'mobilization' and 'activation' (p.13-16 Results; p.16-17 Discussion, paragraph beginning 'We note several new, mode-specific findings among blood transcriptomics').

cohorts.cohort_label: MoTrPAC pre-COVID sedentary adults, baseline acute-bout cohort (EE/RE/CON arms)
cohorts.baseline_health: Healthy, sedentary adults screened and 'medically cleared to be formally randomized'; detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria are not reproduced in this report and are referred to a companion paper (Clinical Landscape, in submission) not retrieved for this pilot — NR for the exact criteria list (e.g., infection exclusion window).
cohorts.age_sex: Overall biospecimen-sampled analytic set (Table 1, N=175): 72% female / 28% male; mean age 41 (SD 15) y; mean BMI 26.9 (SD 4.0) kg/m2. Platform-specific sex/age breakdown by EE/RE/CON in Table S1.
cohorts.training_status: Sedentary/untrained at entry ('healthy but sedentary participants'); randomized to endurance exercise (EE), resistance exercise (RE) or non-exercise control (CON).
cohorts.sport: NA — laboratory cycle-ergometer (EE) or multi-station resistance-machine circuit (RE) acute exercise test; not a sport-specific cohort.
cohorts.cohort_notes: Three candidate denominators are given in the accessible text and are not reconciled: (1) 206 participants 'randomized before the suspension of the MoTrPAC study' (Statistical limitations, p.52); (2) 176 'completed the baseline acute test' (EE=66, RE=73, CON=37) (p.20 STAR Methods); (3) 175 (99%) of those had ≥1 biospecimen sample collected, used as Table 1's 'Overall N' (p.20, p.63). Platform-specific analytic N differ further (Table S1, p.65: transcriptomics N=173 [CON 37/EE 64/RE 72]; proteomics N=44 [CON 12/EE 14/RE 18]; metabolomics N=175 [CON 37/EE 65/RE 73]). See unresolved_questions.
cohorts.age_range: Not reported as a range; reported only as a summary statistic, mean 41 (SD 15) years, overall N=175 (Table 1, p.63).

eligibility_opinion.rationale: R19 reports an identifiable single acute exercise bout (40-min endurance cycling at ~65% VO2peak, or a resistance circuit to volitional fatigue) in healthy sedentary adults, with a pre-exercise baseline, multiple post-exercise blood samples out to 24 h (within the 0-72h organising window), and a concurrent non-exercise control arm (p.5 Abstract; p.21-22 STAR Methods, Acute Exercise Intervention/Biospecimen Collection). Immune linkage is met via a dedicated whole-blood immune-cell transcriptomic enrichment/deconvolution analysis and named immune mediator proteins (granulysin, fractalkine, chemokines/interleukins, granzymes, NK/T-cell receptor transcripts) (p.14 Results heading 'Resistance exercise leads to greater innate immune cellular responses'; p.11,15-16 Results). As a bioRxiv preprint (publication_status=preprint), it belongs in the separate frontier register rather than core peer-reviewed totals, but is charted here with the same extraction fields per contract/manual.

unresolved_questions: Participant-denominator discrepancy: the report gives at least three different overall-cohort numbers that are not reconciled in the accessible text — 206 'randomized before the suspension' (p.53 Statistical limitations), 176 'completed the baseline acute test' (p.20 STAR Methods), and 175 (99%) with >=1 biospecimen collected (p.20; used as Table 1's N). cohorts.n_recruited and report_cohort_links.n_analyzed were both set to UNCLEAR pending human adjudication of which denominator the manual intends as 'n_recruited' vs 'n_analyzed'.

No exact per-timepoint x per-platform x per-group participant n could be located in the main text, Table 1, Table S1/S2 (media-1.xlsx), the Key Resources Table (media-2.docx) or the supplementary figure legends (supplement-3.pdf); only platform-by-group overall N (Table S1) and a qualitative statement that subgroup n can be 'as small as 4 participants' are available. All 14 sample_sets rows therefore carry n_participants = NR at the exact-timepoint level. This is the central calibration question this report's pilot_purpose ('multi-platform different n and repeated samples') was selected to test: should sample_sets rows be created for every group x platform x timepoint combination even when n is unresolvable at that granularity (as done here), or should rows be collapsed to the platform-by-group level when per-timepoint n is unavailable?

Row-unit choice for jointly-reported immune candidates without individual statistics (e.g., M7 chemokine/interleukin group; M8 granzyme family; M9 NK receptor gene set): this pilot used one grouped named_immune_candidate row per jointly-reported set rather than one row per gene/protein, because the source gives no per-feature numeric value outside figure heatmaps that were not digitized. An alternative reading of the manual would split these into one row per named gene/protein with effect_value=NR on each. Needs adjudication.

Text reports NK-cell-marker gene 'KLRK1 (KLRC2)' (p.15), which appears to conflate two distinct HGNC gene symbols; recorded verbatim in M9 rather than corrected, and flagged rather than silently resolved.

Exact blood-transcript timepoint for the RE-unique CD44 increase (M13) is not stated in the main text; only the skeletal-muscle companion timing (3.5 h) is explicit. Linked provisionally to the RE 3.5 h sample_set (SS-R19-09) as the nearest documented timepoint — needs confirmation against Figure S8A-B, which was not digitized in this pass.

Whether a precision_validation row set should be built once per report/cohort (as done here, 7 rows) or once per measurement_id (which would require on the order of 7 x 18 = 126 rows for this report's 18 measurement rows) is not resolved by the manual text consulted; this pilot used the report/cohort-level simplification and flags it for discussion.

No formal full-text screening disposition exists for this pilot item (reports.screening_decision_reviewer_A/B and consensus_screening_decision set to NA rather than NR, since the omission is a scope choice for this charting-only task rather than a reporting gap in the source).

The companion papers repeatedly cited as 'REF, in submission/preparation' (Clinical Landscape, Multi-Omic Landscape, Skeletal Muscle companion, Adipose Tissue companion) were not retrieved; some cohort-level fields (exact eligibility criteria, exact n screened before randomization) may be resolvable only from those companion manuscripts, which are outside this pilot's provided fulltexts.
